context.framing: Treat this as a discrete optimization problem. Objective: minimize calibration ms/event. Surrogate objective: DRAM bytes moved per event (deterministic, statically countable, established as causal). Feasible set: byte-exactness is a binary feasibility gate, never a term traded against speed. Move set, ordered by disturbance: (0) delete no-op astype copies and use out= params; (1) hoist the per-event rebuild of mask, gfac and poff out of pscalib.calib(); (2) relayout constants to (seg,row,col,gain); (3) cache-block the segment loop; (4) take_along_axis in place of np.select; (5) a Numba njit fused kernel. Note moves 2-4 are largely SUBSUMED by move 5 — if you intend to land the Numba kernel, prefer it over spending budget on 2-4. Each accepted move re-ranks the remaining ones, so re-measure every iteration. Theoretical traffic floor is ~250 MB/event against a measured ~6300 MB/event today, so ~25x is the ceiling from traffic reduction alone; Amdahl caps end-to-end cube gain near 20x because psdata's read is ~30 ms/event.
context.preflight: READ .goal/pscalib-calib-speedup.SETUP.md BEFORE any remote command — it holds every machine-dependent fact, and this contract assumes nothing about the machine you are running from. Then verify two HUMAN preconditions, in this order: (1) `command -v bridge bridge-session` must return two paths, else the cc-bridge CLI is not installed here; (2) `timeout 25 ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=15 sdfiana025 hostname` must print sdfiana025, else SSH auth to SLAC is not established. Also confirm the cwd contains the .goal directory holding this contract — the ledger and claims paths below are relative, so a wrong cwd writes them somewhere unintended and the printed digest silently stops matching the file on disk. Neither precondition is fixable by an agent — one needs an install, the other an interactive MFA prompt. If either fails, report the blocker plainly, ask the user to resolve it, and stop; do not spend iterations working around it and do not mark any done_when item met on a machine that cannot reach the remote.
context.bridge: Remote work goes over cc-bridge to sdfiana025; that host is invariant and nothing runs locally. Always start your OWN fresh session and never reuse or assume one — a leftover session may have a different --root-dir, be stale, or be in use, and sessions serialize so sharing one silently blocks you behind another caller. Recipe: `bridge-session start --name pscalib-<purpose> -- ssh sdfiana025 'uv run ~/bridge-server --root-dir /sdf'`, then `bridge --session pscalib-<purpose> status`. Name sessions pscalib-bench / pscalib-src / pscalib-verify, never plain s1 or s2 (those are what a human at a terminal uses). One session runs one command at a time, so start one per concurrent stream of work; stop them with `bridge-session stop <name>` when the iteration ends. Gotchas: `bridge --timeout N` goes BEFORE the subcommand and the local Bash tool has its own 120s limit, so redirect long runs to a remote file and poll; bash output caps at 1MB; a command returning too fast with no output is a broken command, not a negative result.

context.baseline: Measured, 4 arm-runs across sdfmilan053 and sdfmilan046, jungfrau, exp=mfx100848724 run=51, 512 events at 33.5 MB/event: workers=1 gives 1.51-1.66 evt/s (603-658 ms/event); workers=16 gives 8.49-10.58 evt/s at 305-380 MB/s against a 5.54 GB/s node I/O ceiling. Constants are (3,32,512,1024) float32 = 201 MB each for pedestals, pixel_gain, pixel_offset, plus (3,32,512,1024) uint64 = 402 MB pixel_status. No 'mask' constant is supplied, so mask_from_pixel_status runs on every event over the 402 MB uint64 array — the single largest avoidable cost.
context.gate_design: Gate candidates against CURRENT pscalib's own output on real frames, not against psana. Current pscalib is already proven max|diff| == 0 versus det.raw.calib(evt), so equality with it transitively gives equality with psana, and the inner loop then needs no psana environment. Run the full psana gate once, at the end, as the final proof.

operating_mode.role: You are an orchestrator. Each iteration (= one turn): think about the next slice, decompose it, delegate, then integrate and ledger. Every decision is yours — advisors advise, they never decide and never execute. When you overrule an advisor, record the dissent in the ledger rather than deleting it. A worker's report is provenance 'inherited' until you re-verify the artifact yourself; re-verify anything a later iteration will stand on. Prefer the Workflow tool over the Agent tool whenever Workflow is available. The user's approval of this contract authorizes the Workflow tool for delegation, including per-agent model and reasoning-effort overrides.
operating_mode.budget: Delegate to at least 2 and at most 5 subagents per iteration. Advisors convened in an iteration count toward that budget, so shrink the worker count to stay within it.
operating_mode.advisors: planner (opus, xhigh effort) — consulted BEFORE a decomposition is committed, at iteration 1 and at any iteration that changes direction or commits a large share of remaining budget. Mandate: attack the plan; is this the right question, decomposition, stopping rule? Run a pre-mortem naming the most likely way the iteration wastes its budget and the earliest observable sign it is happening. skeptic (opus, xhigh effort) — consulted AFTER results, BEFORE belief, on every iteration that produces a measurement; always a fresh invocation, never the planner. Mandate: refute, not review. Per claim ask: too big or too small to be true? is there an independent cross-check? would the leading alternative mechanism have looked any different? do the books balance? could the check it passed have failed at all? Verdict per claim: BELIEVE, or QUARANTINE with the reason. cold-reader (xhigh effort) — once the deliverable claims to be usable and again after each round of fixes, given the deliverable and NOTHING else: attempt to use it end to end, log every stumble, repair nothing. Workers return evidence, not conclusions: artifacts and identifiers (job ids, SHAs, paths, raw printed output) plus an explicit list of what was NOT done or NOT checked.
operating_mode.discipline: Predict before you measure: write the expected value or band into the ledger BEFORE the measurement runs; a post-hoc band always agrees and proves nothing. Quarantine has teeth: a claim the skeptic rejects is not tagged verified and is not used as a premise later until new evidence resolves the objection. One writer per scarce resource — the candidate worktree, the slurm allocation, the git index — serialize with explicit gates and never assume a queue means free. Advisors receive the evidence and the question, never the answer you hope for.
operating_mode.delegation_guard: Give every worker a cadence with a number in it, so silence is legible as failure and a kill loses little: work in batches of about 12 items, writing results for every id to the output file before starting the next batch, never reading the whole list before writing anything. Poll running agents about every 5 minutes on transcript BYTES, not wall-clock (wall-clock cannot distinguish slow from stuck): trip at 70 MB or at 3x the median sibling. On a trip, SendMessage the agent asking only how many items completed, how many written, which batch, and which item it is reading now. Circling looks like the same items re-read, nothing appended, a plan restated rather than advanced, or an answer naming no number — then TaskStop, keep what it wrote, and relaunch the remainder on a cheaper instrument with a batch cadence rather than the same instrument with a sterner prompt. An agent that has produced no artifact is not still working.
operating_mode.iterations: Complete at least 3 iterations before done_when may be considered met, even if it appears satisfied earlier — use surplus iterations to verify and harden.
operating_mode.ledger: Maintain .goal/pscalib-calib-speedup.ledger.json on disk, appending one FULL entry per iteration: {n, thought, prediction, delegated: [{agent, task, model, effort}], integrated, new, remaining} — the file keeps every field. 'prediction' records the expected value or band written BEFORE any measurement that iteration ran. 'new' must name a decision or artifact that did not exist before this iteration. At the end of EVERY turn print a LEDGER digest (NOT the whole file): a header line `LEDGER pscalib-calib-speedup — iterations N/3, full at .goal/pscalib-calib-speedup.ledger.json` (N = completed-iteration count); then one roster line per completed iteration `n · delegated:k · new: <that iteration's non-empty new>` (k = subagents delegated that iteration); then the current iteration's full JSON entry in a fenced block. Only the printed report shrinks; the file loses nothing. The evaluator reads conversation text only: what this turn's digest does not show does not exist, even if the file does.
operating_mode.claims: Maintain .goal/pscalib-calib-speedup.claims.json on disk — the campaign's key claims (typically 5-15), updated every iteration as claims land or change. Shape: {goal, slug, claims: [{id, provenance, evidence, claim}]} — goal and slug are set at bootstrap, keep them. provenance is one of: verified — evidence cites a checkable artifact you surfaced yourself in this conversation (slurm job id, git SHA, output you printed from your own run); inherited — the evidence you hold is a report rather than the artifact: an external source, or a subagent's account of its own work (name the agent and task). Output a subagent quoted to you stays inherited until you re-run it yourself; inferred — reasoning only (evidence may describe partial support). Tags are lookups against the campaign record, never confidence scores. The final turn prints the complete file via cat.
